podcast.title: Devotional Tour Replacement (1993)
podcast.body: Darryl Bata Montey joined Depeche Mode as a keyboardist, replacing Andy Fletcher for the last 39 shows of the second leg of the Devotional Tour after Fletcher suffered a nervous breakdown. He celebrated his 30th birthday during the tour with a three-day party. "He was replaced on the second leg of the tour by keyboardist Darryl Bata Montey for the last 39 shows."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Introducing "Uncharted": Depeche Mode and the Debauched Devotional Tour

podcast.title: Filled in for Andy Fletcher (1994)
podcast.body: Daryl Bamonte stepped in to replace Andy Fletcher as keyboardist for Depeche Mode during the second leg of their 1994 Exotic Tour, as Fletcher suffered a breakdown. Bamonte covered the entire second leg of the tour, along with six dates in South America. "Bomonte covered the entire second leg of the tour for Andy Fletcher along with six dates in South America."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: We Are The Road Crew - A History of Roadies

podcast.title: Crucial for Tour Completion
podcast.body: Daryl Bamonte's intervention was critical for Depeche Mode, as his willingness to fill in for Andy Fletcher enabled the band to complete one of the biggest tours of their career, which would otherwise have been cut short. "Without him, Depeche mode would not have been able to finish one of the biggest tours of their career."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: We Are The Road Crew - A History of Roadies

podcast.title: Long-time Road Crew Member for Depeche Mode
podcast.body: Daryl Bamonte had been a part of Depeche Mode's road crew since the early days of the band, indicating a deep familiarity with their operations and music. "His place was taken by Darrell Bomonte, who had been working as part of Depeche modes road crew since the early days."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: We Are The Road Crew - A History of Roadies

xref.title: Breakdown on Exotic Tour (1994)
xref.body: During Depeche Mode's 1994 Exotic Tour, which became known for its debauchery, Andy Fletcher experienced a breakdown two months into the tour and was forced to return home. His role was then taken over by Daryl Bamonte, who had been part of Depeche Mode's road crew since their early days. "Depeche survived two months before he had a breakdown and needed to go home."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: We Are The Road Crew - A History of Roadies

xref.title: Guitar Tech for The Cure
xref.body: Perry Bamonte, brother of Daryl Bamonte (who filled in for Depeche Mode), started his career as a guitar tech for The Cure. "Perry Bimonte, the brother of the affirmation Darrell Bimonte who bailed out Depeche mode in 1994 started as a guitar tech for the cure."
